mainTopic: The laws of זימון: whether two may make one, counting an absent diner, who must pause for whom, and answering אמן.
overview: This amud deals with the rules of זימון. It first asks whether two people who ate together may make a זימון if they want to. A proof from women making a זימון is rejected, because three women are still three separate people (דעות). The גמרא then shows that רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids a זימון of two, while רב allows it. Next it explains רב's ruling about a diner who stepped out to the market. He counts only if he hears and answers (אביי), and for a זימון of ten he must actually come back (מר זוטרא), because ה׳'s Name is mentioned. Further rules follow: two diners should bless separately unless one is unlearned, and one diner must pause for two but two need not pause for one. A story with מרימר teaches that three equals must still make a זימון, and that a זימון cannot be made after the fact. The amud ends with what a latecomer answers to a זימון, and with saying אמן after one's own ברכה of בונה ירושלים.

steps.title: Finishing the rejection of the waiter proof
steps.stepSummary: The previous proof from the שמש is pushed aside. In that case, the people prefer to make their זימון a real obligation from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they prefer to set up their זימון as an obligation right from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes rejecting the previous proof. It explains why the case of the waiter does not prove that two can make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone tried to prove from the case of a שמש (waiter) that two may make a זימון voluntarily. The גמרא answers that there, the people want their זימון to be a full חובה from the outset, not an optional רשות. So that case says nothing about a voluntary זימון of two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is preferable to them; they want it
To establish, to set up permanently
From the start, from the outset

phrases.english: because it is preferable to them
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence that began on the previous page.

phrases.english: to establish it for themselves as an obligation from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּנִיחָא לְהוּ דְּמַקְבַּע לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the rejection of the previous proof (from the waiter case), which began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the waiter case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the waiter case the people choose to make the זימון a חובה from the start, so it is not a model for a voluntary זימון of two.

steps.title: Quoting a ברייתא about women and slaves making a זימון
steps.stepSummary: A new proof begins. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: women may make a זימון by themselves, and slaves may make a זימון by themselves. But women, slaves, and children together may not, even if they want to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Women make a זימון for themselves, and slaves make a זימון for themselves. Women, slaves, and minors, if they want to make a זימון together, they do not make a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to prove that two can make a זימון. This step only quotes the source; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts. The רישא says each group (women alone, or slaves alone) may make a זימון. The סיפא says a mixed group of women, slaves, and minors may not. Both parts will matter: the proof uses the רישא, and the later challenge uses the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: They make a זימון (the group invitation to ברכת המזון)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts of the ברייתא. Women ALONE may make a זימון. Women, slaves, and minors TOGETHER may not.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Women form a zimmun for themselves,
and slaves form a zimmun for themselves,
women, slaves, and minors
if they wish to form a zimmun together, they may not form a zimmun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the waiter proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That two men may make a זימון voluntarily.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about women and slaves making a זימון.

steps.title: The proof: women count like two men, yet they may make a זימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the proof. Even 100 women count only like two men, yet the ברייתא lets women make a זימון. So two men should also be able to make one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even a hundred women are considered like two men. And yet the ברייתא teaches that women make a זימון for themselves and slaves make a זימון for themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא proves that two men can make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a group of women, however large, counts no more than two men. Two men are not enough for the standard זימון of three. If women may still make a זימון, then a group with the strength of only two men can make a זימון. So two actual men should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that: introduces a known fact used in an argument

phrases.english: But aren't women, even a hundred
phrases.notes: Some versions seem to say this twice, once here and again in the next phrase; the meaning is the same.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מְאָה נָשֵׁי כִּתְרֵי גַּבְרֵי דָּמְיָין,
phrases.english: but aren't a hundred women considered like two men,
and yet it teaches: women form a zimmun for themselves
and slaves form a zimmun for themselves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מְאָה נָשֵׁי כִּתְרֵי גַּבְרֵי דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רישא of the ברייתא from step 2 to build the argument.
steps.raayaObject: That two men may make a זימון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the ברייתא, together with the principle that 100 women are like two men.

steps.title: Rejection: three women are still three separate people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Women are different, because a group of three women is three separate minds (דעות). Two men are only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because there are separate minds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'like two men' is about how women count in certain contexts. It does not erase the fact that three women are three individuals. A זימון needs separate people who can invite one another to praise ה׳. Three women have that, but two men do not, so the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: a standard formula for rejecting a comparison

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of דעות becomes the key issue. It is the basis for the attack in the next step.

phrases.english: There it is different, because there are separate minds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between women making a זימון and two men making a זימון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Women, even if they count as 'two men' in some ways, are still three separate people, which a זימון requires. Two men are only two people.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the ברייתא: why can't a mixed group make a זימון?
steps.stepSummary: If separate minds are enough, then women and slaves together should be able to make a זימון. Yet the סיפא of the ברייתא says they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: women and slaves, if they want to make a זימון, they do not make a זימון. Why not? There are separate minds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 4 using the second half of the same ברייתא. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said three separate people are enough for a זימון. A mixed group of women and slaves is also made of separate people. So the סיפא, which forbids them, seems to contradict the reasoning of 'there are separate minds.'

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge based on what was just said
Say the end clause, look at the last part of the source

steps.whatToRemember: The flow so far: the proof from women (they count like two men, yet make a זימון) was rejected with the idea of 'separate minds.' Now that idea is challenged from the סיפא, which forbids women and slaves together.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין.
phrases.english: Women and slaves, if they wish to form a zimmun, may not form a zimmun.
Why not? But there are separate minds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning 'שאני התם דאיכא דעות' from step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If separate minds are enough for a זימון, a mixed group of women and slaves also has separate minds. So the סיפא's ruling that they may not make a זימון seems to contradict that reasoning.

steps.title: Women and slaves are kept apart for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: Women and slaves may not make a זימון together because of concern for immoral behavior (פריצותא). The reason is not a lack of separate minds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because of concern for immoral behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. Women and slaves may not join together for a זימון for a separate reason: the חכמים worried about improper closeness between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked why women and slaves together cannot make a זימון if 'separate minds' are enough. The answer is that the 'separate minds' logic still works. The סיפא of the ברייתא forbids this mix only as a protective rule against פריצותא. So the רישא still shows that three separate minds can make a זימון, and two men are still only two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case has its own reason
Immoral or improper behavior; lack of modesty

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer means women and slaves 'don't count' for a זימון. Each group alone may make one. Only mixing them is forbidden, and the reason is protective, not about counting.

phrases.english: It is different there
phrases.notes: Referring to the סיפא: women and slaves together

phrases.english: because of immoral behavior.
phrases.notes: This rule is there to protect against bad behavior, not to say who counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 and protects the דחיה of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying reason (סברא) for the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on women and slaves joining shows that separate minds are not enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban exists only because of concern for פריצותא; separate minds remain a valid reason for women to make a זימון.

steps.title: Trying to show that רב is the one who forbids two from making a זימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב holds 'even if they want, they may not make a זימון', and quotes רב's ruling about three who ate together when one went out to the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it is רב who said: if they wanted to make a זימון, they may not. For רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רב: three who ate together, and one of them went out to the market, call him back and make the זימון including him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: in the מחלוקת between רב and רבי יוחנן, which of them holds that two may not make a זימון? It quotes a ruling of רב to set up a proof, and draws the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that רב and רבי יוחנן argue, but we did not know who held which view. Here the גמרא brings a source from רב about three people where one stepped out. The proof itself comes in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude; let us establish (introduces an attempt to settle who said what)
If they wanted to make a זימון

steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing which אמורא holds which view lets us apply their other rulings consistently and decide the הלכה.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is רב who said
phrases.notes: Opens the question of who said which view

phrases.english: if they wanted to make a זימון, they may not make a זימון.
phrases.notes: About two people who ate together

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: For רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רב:
phrases.notes: The source for the proof

phrases.english: Three who ate together
and one of them went out to the market —
they call him and make the זימון including him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line: identifying the speakers in the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds two may not make a זימון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling, quoted by רב דימי בר יוסף, about three who ate when one went to the market

steps.title: Drawing the inference from רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: They can make the זימון only because they call him back. Without him, the two who remain could not make one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that they call him; but if they do not call him, no, they cannot make a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads an inference into רב's words. Only by calling the third person back can they make a זימון, so two alone cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two could make a זימון whenever they wanted, why would רב need them to call back the third? The two remaining could just make it themselves. So רב must hold that two may not make a זימון.

phrases.english: The reason is that they call him,
but if they do not call him — no!
phrases.notes: Implies two alone cannot make a זימון

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּקוֹרְאִין לוֹ, הָא לֹא קוֹרְאִין לוֹ — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that Step 7 set up.
steps.raayaObject: רב holds two may not make a זימון

steps.title: That group was fixed as an obligated three from the start
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Those three ate as an obligated group of three, so they must include the third person, which says nothing about two who ate alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because they were set as an obligation from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof about רב. That case involved a group that started as three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the three began eating together, they became a group with a real חיוב of זימון. So their זימון must be done as that group of three, including the one who left. Even if רב allows two to make a voluntary זימון, these people must still call back the third.

keyTerms.meaning: They were established; set in place

phrases.english: It is different there
because they were set as an obligated group from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאִקְּבַעוּ לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Steps 7–8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof; does not decide what רב actually holds
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case had a fixed obligation of three from the start, unlike two who ate alone

steps.title: Trying instead to show that רבי יוחנן forbids two from making a זימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests that רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids it, and quotes his ruling that one of two diners can be יוצא through the other's ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, conclude that it is רבי יוחנן who said: if they wanted to make a זימון, they may not. For רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: two who ate together, one of them can be יוצא with his friend's ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proof about רב fell, the גמרא tries the other side: maybe רבי יוחנן holds that two may not make a זימון. This step sets up the proof, which steps 11–13 complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that when two ate together, one can be יוצא through the other's ברכה. The point the גמרא will draw out is that רבי יוחנן only mentions hearing the friend's ברכה, not making a זימון. That suggests two cannot make a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; instead (switching to the other possibility)

phrases.english: Rather, conclude that it is רבי יוחנן
phrases.notes: Now the גמרא tries it the other way around: who said which view.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין,
phrases.english: who said: if they wanted to make a זימון, they may not,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
two who ate together —
one of them fulfills his obligation with his friend's ברכה.
phrases.notes: Only hearing the ברכה is mentioned, not a זימון

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תִּסְתַּיֵּים, דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רב is rejected, it tries the opposite identification.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds two may not make a זימון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling, quoted by רבה בר בר חנה, that one of two diners is יוצא through the other's ברכה

steps.title: What new point is רבי יוחנן teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say that one of two diners can be יוצא through the other's ברכה, since a ברייתא already teaches that hearing a ברכה without answering is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: What is he teaching us? We already learned: one who heard a ברכה and did not answer has fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling as seemingly obvious. This question sets up the next step, where his real point is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that just hearing a ברכה is enough to be יוצא. So if רבי יוחנן only meant that one diner can be יוצא through the other's ברכה, he added nothing new. His statement must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it / we raised a question about it
What is he teaching us? (What is the new point?)
One who heard and did not answer has still fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
One who heard and did not answer has fulfilled his obligation!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the רבי יוחנן ruling quoted in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that one of two diners can be יוצא through the other's ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the rule that hearing a ברכה is enough is already known from a ברייתא

steps.title: רבי זירא: two diners have no זימון
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבי יוחנן's point is that two people have no ברכת הזימון between them. They can only be יוצא through one person's ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: He is teaching that there is no ברכת הזימון among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question by showing what new point רבי יוחנן was really making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not that hearing works. It is that two diners can only share a ברכה by listening; they cannot make a זימון together. By saying 'one is יוצא through the other' instead of 'they make a זימון', רבי יוחנן shows that a זימון is not available for two.

keyTerms.meaning: The invitation-blessing said when a group joins together for ברכת המזון
Among them / between the two of them

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
It comes to say that there is no blessing of zimmun among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין בִּרְכַּת הַזִּימּוּן בֵּינֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was just repeating that hearing a ברכה is enough
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן is teaching that two diners cannot make a זימון

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן holds that two may not make a זימון even if they want to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, conclude from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the search begun earlier. The strict opinion belongs to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 to 9 tried to pin the strict view on רב and failed. רבי זירא's explanation now shows that רבי יוחנן is the one who rules out a זימון for two.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that two people who ate together cannot make a זימון, even if they want to. One can only be יוצא by hearing the other's ברכה.

phrases.english: Conclude it (it is proven).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof begun in Step 10
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן is the אמורא who says that two may not make a זימון even if they want to

steps.title: The Sages from ארץ ישראל allow it
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא challenges his father: the Sages who came from ארץ ישראל reported that two may make a זימון if they want. Surely they heard this from רבי יוחנן, the great teacher of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said to רב הונא: But the Sages who came from the West (ארץ ישראל) say that if two want to make a זימון, they may. Isn't it that they heard this from רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge pushes back against the conclusion that רבי יוחנן holds the strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was the leading teacher in ארץ ישראל. So a lenient ruling brought from there seems to come from him, which would contradict Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who came from the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
If they want to make a זימון, they may
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested proof)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna said to Rav Huna:
But the Sages who came from the West say:
If they wanted to make a zimmun, they may make one.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דִּשְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: Is it not that they heard it from Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יוחנן forbids a זימון for two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lenient ruling reported from ארץ ישראל was likely heard from רבי יוחנן

steps.title: They heard it from רב before he left
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the Sages may have heard the lenient ruling from רב while he was still in ארץ ישראל, before he went down to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, they heard it from רב, before he went down to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against the challenge by offering a different source for the lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב also studied in ארץ ישראל before moving to בבל, so the ruling need not come from רבי יוחנן. The conclusion that רבי יוחנן is strict stands, and רב can be the lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: Before he went down to Babylonia

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the split intact: רב allows two to make a זימון if they wish, and רבי יוחנן does not.

phrases.english: No, they heard it from Rav,
before he went down to Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lenient ruling from ארץ ישראל came from רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: It came from רב during his time in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: Calling back a diner who went out to the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's ruling quoted earlier: if three ate together and one stepped out to the market, the others call him and include him in the זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רב: Three who ate together, and one went out to the market, they call him and make the זימון including him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the argument and turns to explaining רב's ruling from Step 7 on its own terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא signals that the גמרא is now studying a statement it quoted earlier for a proof. The basic rule is that a diner who stepped away can still be counted in the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: Who ate together as one group
And they make the זימון including him

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Yosef said that Rav said:
Three who ate together,
and one of them went out to the market,
they call him and include him in the zimmun.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling of רב quoted in Step 7, now to analyze it directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one of three diners stepped out, the others call him and count him in the זימון

steps.title: אביי: only if he hears and answers
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits רב's ruling: the absent diner counts only if they call him and he answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And this is only when they call him and he answers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a condition to רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling out to him is not enough by itself. He must be close enough to hear and respond, so that he actually takes part in the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (introduces a limiting condition)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And that is when they call him and he answers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהוּא דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְעָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to רב's ruling in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The absent diner counts only if he hears the call and answers

steps.title: מר זוטרא: for ten, he must come back
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא limits the ruling further: answering from afar works only for a זימון of three. For a זימון of ten, the absent diner must come back and sit with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: We said this only about three. But for ten, they must wait until he comes back.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds a second limit, based on the size of the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זימון of ten includes mentioning ה׳'s name, so it is treated more strictly. For three, hearing and answering is enough. For ten, the missing person must physically return before they can make the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: With ten (a זימון that mentions ה׳'s name)

steps.whatToRemember: Calling back a diner who stepped out works only if he hears and answers (אביי), and only for a זימון of three. For ten, he must actually return (מר זוטרא).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is the same for every size of group. Answering from a distance works for three but not for ten.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
We said this only about three,
but with ten, not until he comes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further limits רב's ruling, after אביי's condition in Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answering from a distance counts only for a זימון of three; for ten, the absent diner must return

steps.title: רב אשי argues the opposite makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא. He says nine people already look like ten, so a missing tenth is less important. But two people do not look like three, so the third should have to be physically present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenges this: On the contrary, the reverse makes more sense. Nine look like ten, but two do not look like three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks מר זוטרא's ruling from step 18. He argues that the strict rule should apply to three, not to ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא said that answering from afar works for three, but not for ten. רב אשי says that in a big group of nine, one missing person is barely noticed, so the group still looks like ten. In a group of two, a missing third is very obvious, so it makes more sense to require him to sit with them.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenges it:
On the contrary, the reverse makes more sense:
nine look like ten,
phrases.notes: In a large group, one missing person is hardly noticed.

phrases.english: two do not look like three.
phrases.notes: In a small group, one missing person is obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אַדְּרַבָּא אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's distinction between three and ten
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's rule that answering from afar works for three but not for ten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Common sense says it should be the reverse. Nine already look like ten, but two never look like three, so the stricter rule belongs to three.

steps.title: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא because God's Name is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like מר זוטרא. The reason is that a זימון of ten mentions שם שמים, and it is not proper to do that with fewer than ten people actually present.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows מר זוטרא. What is the reason? Since they need to mention the Name of Heaven, it is not proper conduct to do so with fewer than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument in favor of מר זוטרא and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's argument was about how the group looks. The גמרא answers with a different factor: in a זימון of ten, the leader adds God's Name. Mentioning God's Name needs a real group of ten sitting together. A זימון of three does not mention God's Name, so there is room to be lenient there.
steps.whatToRemember: For a זימון of three, a diner who stepped out counts if they call him and he answers. For a זימון of ten, he must come back and sit with them, because God's Name is mentioned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה for counting an absent diner toward a זימון of ten.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Mar Zutra.
What is the reason?
Since they need to mention the Name of Heaven,
phrases.notes: In a זימון of ten, the leader adds God's Name.

phrases.english: with fewer than ten, it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's argument and rules like מר זוטרא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows מר זוטרא. A זימון of ten mentions God's Name, so all ten must be physically present.

steps.title: אביי: two who ate together should bless separately
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: when two people eat together, it is a מצוה for them to split up and each say ברכת המזון himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that two who ate together have a מצוה to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about זימון rules. אביי says that two diners should each bless on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people are not enough for a real זימון. Instead of one blessing on behalf of the other, each should say his own ברכת המזון. This fits the view against a זימון of two, which steps 10–13 tied to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (literally, we hold)
It is a מצוה to separate (each blesses alone)

steps.confusionAlert: "Separate" does not mean they must get up and leave. It means each one says his own ברכת המזון instead of one saying it for both.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
two who ate together,
it is a מצוה for them to separate.
phrases.notes: Each recites his own ברכת המזון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New teaching on זימון after the previous topic was closed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two who ate together should each say ברכת המזון separately.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing as אביי: two who ate together have a מצוה to separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Two who ate together have a מצוה to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what אביי said, which supports his tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's statement is now backed by a תנאי source, not just an oral tradition. The ברייתא continues in the next step with an important limit.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
Two who ate together, it is a מצוה for them to separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: אביי's tradition that two diners should bless separately
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the identical wording

steps.title: Exception: a learned person can bless for an unlearned one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule. Splitting up applies only when both people are learned. If one is learned and the other is not, the learned one blesses and the other fulfills his obligation by listening.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When both are learned. But if one is learned and one is unlearned, the learned one blesses and the unlearned one fulfills his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds an exception to the rule of separating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating only makes sense when both can say ברכת המזון themselves. If one cannot, he is better off listening to the learned person's ברכה and fulfilling his obligation through him. The rule still applies; this is a special case of how it is carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (introduces a limit)
A learned person who can say the ברכות

steps.whatToRemember: Two diners each bless on their own, unless one is unlearned. Then the learned one blesses for both.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When both of them are learned,
but if one is learned and one is unlearned,
the learned one blesses, and the unlearned one fulfills his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא limits its own rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separating applies only when both are learned. A learned person blesses on behalf of an unlearned one.

steps.title: רבא: one stops eating for two, but two do not stop for one
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches, and says רבי זירא was quoted the same way: if three ate together, one diner must stop eating to join the other two for a זימון, but two do not have to stop for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I said this myself, and it was stated in the name of רבי זירא like me. Three who ate together: one interrupts his meal for the two, but two do not interrupt for the one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about three diners who are not finishing at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two want to bless and the third is still eating, he must pause so they can make a זימון. The majority's wish wins. If only one wants to bless, the other two do not have to stop their meal for him. רבא also notes that רבי זירא was quoted saying the same thing.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This matter, I said it myself,
and it was stated in the name of Rabbi Zeira in agreement with me:
three who ate together,
one interrupts his meal for the two,
phrases.notes: If two want to bless, the third stops eating to join the זימון.

phrases.english: but two do not interrupt their meal for the one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא מִילְּתָא אַמְרִיתָא אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New זימון rule about diners who finish at different times
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Among three diners, one must pause his meal so the other two can make a זימון, but two need not pause for one.

steps.title: Challenge from רב פפא stopping for his son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that two do not stop for one. רב פפא, together with one other person, stopped eating so that his son אבא מר could join a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do two really not stop for one? But רב פפא stopped for his son אבא מר, and it was רב פפא and one other person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 24, that two people do not have to stop eating for one. It points to a real case where two did stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said only one person must stop to join two. Here, רב פפא and another person (two people) stopped their meal for one person, his son. That looks like an action that goes against רבא's rule.

phrases.english: And do they not? But Rav Pappa
phrases.notes: וְהָא introduces a challenge from a known case

phrases.english: stopped (his meal) for Abba Mar his son
phrases.notes: He interrupted eating so his son could join a זימון

phrases.english: he and one other!
phrases.notes: Two people stopped for one, the opposite of רבא's rule

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא אַפְסֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבא's rule in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that two do not have to stop eating for one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מעשה (actual case) shows two people stopping for one, which suggests that two must stop after all.

steps.title: רב פפא went beyond the letter of the law
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's case is different. He did more than the law requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא is different, because he acted beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב פפא was not required to stop. He chose to do extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 24 stays in place: two are not obligated to stop for one. רב פפא's action was a voluntary extra step, so it proves nothing about what the law requires.

keyTerms.meaning: beyond the letter of the law; doing more than required

steps.whatToRemember: Two people are not required to stop eating for one. Doing so is a praiseworthy extra (לפנים משורת הדין).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa is different,
for it was beyond the letter of the law that he acted.
phrases.notes: His action was voluntary, not obligatory

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a voluntary act, not the basic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's behavior shows that two must stop for one
steps.terutzMaskana: He did extra on his own. The law still says two need not stop.

steps.title: Story setup: three equal חכמים eat together
steps.stepSummary: Three חכמים ate bread together, and none of them stood out above the others as the obvious one to lead the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בר מרימר, מר בר רב אשי, and רב אחא from Difti ate bread together. None of them was greater than his fellows, so no one was the clear choice to bless for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This line only sets up the situation for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that all three were equal. That detail is what creates the question in the next step about whether the זימון rule applies to them.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר וּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Yehuda bar Mareimar and Mar bar Rav Ashi
and Rav Aḥa of Difti
ate bread together,
there was not among them one
who was greater than his fellow
to bless for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר וּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי וְרַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about how the obligation of זימון applies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: three equals ate together, and none of them was the natural leader.

steps.title: Does זימון apply when no one is greater?
steps.stepSummary: The three asked whether the משנה's obligation of זימון applies only when a great person is present. If all are equal, perhaps separate ברכות are better.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat and asked: The משנה says three who ate together must make a זימון. Maybe that applies only when there is a great person among them. But when they are all equal, maybe it is better to split up and each say his own ברכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים raise a question about the scope of the משנה. They ask whether the חיוב of זימון depends on having a leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says three who eat together 'must' make a זימון. They suggest the rule might assume someone suitable to lead. Without such a person, splitting up (like the two in steps 21-23) might be the better choice.

keyTerms.meaning: splitting up the ברכות (each says his own)

phrases.english: They sat and it was a question for them:
That which we learned: three who ate together
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: are obligated to make a zimmun,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא אָדָם גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: does that apply only where there is a great person,
but where they are equal to each other —
splitting the blessings is preferable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the question that the setup in step 27 led to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the obligation of זימון apply even when all three diners are equal?

steps.title: Each one blessed for himself
steps.stepSummary: The three acted on their doubt. Each said ברכת המזון on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each person blessed for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Following their idea that splitting up is better, they did not make a זימון, and each one blessed alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is what they did in practice, based on the side of their question that said separate ברכות are better. It sets up the next step, where they ask מרימר whether they acted correctly.

phrases.english: Each person blessed for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how they acted on their question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, they split up and did not make a זימון.

steps.title: מרימר: you fulfilled the ברכה, but not the זימון
steps.stepSummary: מרימר ruled that they fulfilled ברכת המזון but missed their obligation of זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before מרימר. He said to them: You fulfilled the obligation of the ברכה, but you did not fulfill the obligation of זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The three ask מרימר, and he tells them that splitting up was wrong. They still had to make a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרימר rejects their idea. The משנה's obligation of זימון applies even when all three are equal, and it does not depend on having a great person present. Their individual ברכות counted for ברכת המזון, but the separate מצוה of זימון was lost.

keyTerms.meaning: you fulfilled the obligation of the blessing

steps.confusionAlert: ברכת המזון and זימון are two separate obligations. You can fulfill the first and still miss the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches the הלכה: three who eat together must make a זימון even if none of them is greater than the others.

phrases.english: They came before Mareimar.
He said to them: You fulfilled the obligation of blessing,
you did not fulfill the obligation of zimmun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and judges the action in step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obligation of זימון applies even among equals. Splitting up made them lose the זימון.

steps.title: A זימון cannot be made after the fact
steps.stepSummary: מרימר adds that they cannot go back now and make a זימון, because there is no retroactive זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Let us go back and make a זימון, there is no retroactive זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר answers a suggestion before they even make it. They cannot fix the mistake by making a זימון now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זימון is an introduction to ברכת המזון. Once ברכת המזון has already been said, the opening has no purpose, so it cannot be added afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: let us go back and make a זימון

steps.whatToRemember: Three who ate together must make a זימון even if they are equal, and once each has blessed alone, the זימון cannot be made up.

phrases.english: And if you say: Let us go back and make a zimmun,
there is no retroactive zimmun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to מרימר's ruling by closing off any way to make up the זימון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זימון cannot be done after ברכת המזון has already been said.

steps.title: What does a latecomer answer to a זימון?
steps.stepSummary: Someone arrives while a group is in the middle of the זימון. What should he answer after them?
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone came and found them in the middle of blessing, what does he say after them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a person who did not eat with the group but hears them making the זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person is not part of the זימון because he did not eat with them. The question is what response fits for someone who is only listening in.

keyTerms.meaning: what does he say after them?

phrases.english: He came and found them while they were blessing,
what does he say after them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new question about זימון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper response for a non-participant who hears a זימון

steps.title: רב זביד: he says ברוך ומבורך
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the latecomer responds with 'ברוך ומבורך', meaning 'Blessed is He and blessed is His Name forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: He says 'Blessed and blessed'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the latecomer question. He says a short praise similar to what the group says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב זביד, the latecomer may join in with words of praise. He cannot say the group's actual response, because he did not eat, so he says a general blessing of ה׳'s Name instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed is He and blessed (is His Name)', a short praise

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: "Blessed and blessed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to step 32

steps.title: רב פפא: he answers אמן
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the latecomer simply answers אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He answers 'אמן'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second answer. The latecomer only answers אמן to what he hears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that a non-participant should not add his own words of praise. He just affirms the ברכה by answering אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: he answers אמן (affirming what he heard)

steps.confusionAlert: This רב פפא is the same name as in step 25, but here he is giving a separate opinion on a completely different question.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: He answers "amen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion that disagrees with רב זביד in step 33

steps.title: Both opinions are correct, at different moments of the זימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reconciles רב זביד and רב פפא by assigning each ruling to a different point in the זימון. If the latecomer hears the leader say 'נברך', he answers 'ברוך ומבורך'. If he hears the group answering 'ברוך', he just says אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't really disagree. One ruling is for when he arrived and heard them saying 'Let us bless.' The other is for when he arrived and heard them saying 'Blessed.' If he heard 'Let us bless,' he says 'Blessed is He and blessed is His Name.' If he heard 'Blessed,' he answers אמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב זביד and רב פפא are not arguing. Each is describing a different moment when the latecomer walks in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the latecomer arrives while the leader is still inviting ('נברך'), he answers that invitation with his own words of praise, 'ברוך ומבורך'. He does not say the diners' own response, since he did not eat with them. If he arrives once they are already at 'ברוך', the invitation is over, and all he can add is אמן. Both rulings are true; they simply apply at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree. This signals that two opinions will be reconciled.
He found them, meaning he arrived while they were saying a certain part.
'Let us bless.' This is the leader's invitation in the זימון.
'Blessed is He and blessed [is His Name].' This is the latecomer's response.

steps.whatToRemember: Latecomer to a זימון: if he hears the invitation 'נברך', he says 'ברוך ומבורך'. If he hears the response 'ברוך', he says אמן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא rejects saying 'ברוך ומבורך'. Each אמורא is simply talking about a different moment of arrival.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.
This one is where he found them saying 'Let us bless.'
phrases.notes: This is רב זביד's case.

phrases.english: And that one is where he found them saying 'Blessed.'
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's case.

phrases.english: If he found them saying 'Let us bless,'
he says 'Blessed is He and blessed [is His Name].'
If he found them saying 'Blessed,'
he answers 'Amen.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Harmonizes the two answers given in steps 33 and 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רב זביד and רב פפא disagree about the correct response.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruling applies at a different moment of the זימון, so there is no dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing 'נברך' means answering 'ברוך ומבורך'. Hearing 'ברוך' means answering אמן.

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict each other about answering אמן to your own ברכה
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says answering אמן after your own ברכות is praiseworthy. Another ברייתא says it is improper. This sets up a contradiction for the גמרא to resolve.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: someone who answers אמן after his own blessings is praiseworthy. Another ברייתא teaches: that is disgraceful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to say opposite things. This is setting up the next step, where the contradiction will be resolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות describe the exact same act: answering אמן after your own ברכה. Yet one praises it and the other condemns it. Something must be different between the cases, and the next step will identify what it is.

phrases.english: One [ברייתא] taught:
One who answers 'Amen' after his own blessings,
this is praiseworthy.
And another [ברייתא] taught:
This is disgraceful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic about answering אמן, this time after one's own ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same act cannot be both praiseworthy and disgraceful unless the cases differ.

steps.title: Answering אמן is good after בונה ירושלים but improper after other ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved by case. Answering אמן to yourself is praiseworthy after בונה ירושלים and improper after other ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the ברכה of 'Who builds Jerusalem.' That one is about the other blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בונה ירושלים is the last of the main ברכות of ברכת המזון. Saying אמן there marks the end of that core unit, so it is praiseworthy. After other ברכות, answering אמן to yourself is out of place, so it is improper.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This introduces a resolution.
'Who builds Jerusalem.' This is the third ברכה of ברכת המזון.

steps.whatToRemember: One answers אמן after his own ברכה of בונה ירושלים in ברכת המזון, but not after his other ברכות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of saying אמן after בונה ירושלים in ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This is about 'Who builds Jerusalem.'
phrases.notes: Here it is praiseworthy.

phrases.english: That is about the other blessings.
phrases.notes: Here it is disgraceful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the two ברייתות give opposite rulings for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The praiseworthy case is בונה ירושלים. The improper case is other ברכות.

steps.title: אביי said the אמן loudly so the workers could go back to work
steps.stepSummary: אביי answered אמן aloud after בונה ירושלים. This let workers know they could leave, since הטוב והמטיב is not a Torah-level obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would answer it aloud, so that the workers would hear and get up [to return to work], because 'Who is good and does good' is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how אביי practiced the rule from the previous step: he said the אמן after בונה ירושלים out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three ברכות of ברכת המזון are דאורייתא. הטוב והמטיב was added later by the חכמים. Workers are allowed to skip it so they don't lose their employer's time. אביי's loud אמן signaled that the Torah-level part was over and the workers could leave.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good.' This is the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: Abaye would answer it aloud,
phrases.notes: He answered the אמן after בונה ירושלים.

phrases.english: so that the workers would hear and get up,
because 'Who is good and does good' is not from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how אביי carried out the ruling of step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי said the אמן after בונה ירושלים aloud, to let workers leave before the rabbinic ברכה of הטוב והמטיב.

steps.title: רב אשי said the אמן quietly so people would not belittle הטוב והמטיב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי whispered his אמן after בונה ירושלים. He did not want people to treat הטוב והמטיב as unimportant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי would answer it in a whisper, so that people would not treat 'Who is good and does good' lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts אביי with רב אשי, who said the same אמן quietly for the opposite concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי worried that a loud אמן would make the fourth ברכה look optional or unimportant. Both אמוראים agree that the אמן is said; they differ only on whether to say it loudly. אביי focused on the workers' needs, and רב אשי focused on protecting the honor of הטוב והמטיב.

keyTerms.meaning: They would treat [it] lightly or belittle [it].

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone says אמן after בונה ירושלים. אביי said it loudly to help workers, and רב אשי said it quietly to protect the importance of הטוב והמטיב.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi would answer it in a whisper,
so that people would not treat lightly
'Who is good and does good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting practice to אביי's in step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי whispered the אמן after בונה ירושלים so that הטוב והמטיב would not be belittled.
